entries.term: it-cleft with not until: It wasn't until … that …

entries.term: contrastive it-cleft: It's not the money that …, it's …

entries.term: It's not that …, it's just that …

entries.term: wh-cleft with an adjective: What's interesting is that …

entries.term: wh-cleft with happen: What happened was …

entries.term: reversed wh-cleft: This is where … / That's where X comes in

entries.term: Not that …: Not that it matters, but …

entries.term: inverted exclamative: Boy, was I wrong!

entries.term: No way + inversion: No way am I paying that

entries.term: There goes …: There goes my weekend

very strong 'I have never'; formal or dramatic

states a strict condition; inversion is in the main clause
absolute prohibition; used in rules and warnings
never, at any moment; common in statements and news
strong denial: not at all, in any respect
says one place or case shows something most clearly
adds a second negative clause; the auxiliary comes before the subject

entries.term: as + inversion: …, as did most of the board
entries.gloss: says that others did the same; common in news writing
makes the previous statement stronger and adds its result

entries.term: no inversion with pronouns: Here it comes / There she goes
entries.gloss: nouns invert after here and there; pronoun subjects do not

entries.term: fronted participle + inversion: Gone are the days when …
entries.gloss: says that something belongs to the past
fronted participle with inversion in emails and letters

entries.term: fronted comparative + inversion: More important is …
entries.gloss: starts with the comparison to add a stronger point

entries.term: fronted prepositional phrase + inversion: Of particular concern is …
entries.gloss: puts the topic first in formal reports

entries.term: it-cleft on a phrase: It was in Berlin that …
entries.gloss: stresses a time, place or reason with It is … that

entries.term: wh-cleft with do: What we did was …
entries.gloss: focuses on an action; the verb after was is often bare
explains a cause; avoid 'the reason is because' in writing
focuses on the exact point of disagreement or failure

entries.term: The last thing … is …: The last thing we need is …

strongly highlights a single lesson, fact or quality

entries.term: cleft question: What is it about … that …?

one thing happened just after another; formal narrative

parts.title: Conditionals, wishes & hypothetical meaning
parts.deck: kizamu-english::C2::10 Advanced grammar::02 Conditionals, wishes & hypothetical meaning

entries.term: mixed conditional: past condition → present result (If I had taken it, I'd be … now)

entries.term: inverted conditional: Should you have any questions, …

entries.term: say / let's say (= suppose): Say you lost your job …
entries.gloss: introduces an imagined situation in conversation

entries.term: what if + past (suggestion): What if we tried …?
entries.gloss: makes a polite suggestion or imagines an unreal situation

entries.term: in case vs. if: Take a jacket in case it gets cold

entries.term: wish + past perfect: I wish I had …

entries.term: would rather + past (other subject): I'd rather you didn't

entries.term: like as a conjunction: It looks like it's going to rain

entries.term: X, if not Y: hundreds, if not thousands

entries.term: past tense for politeness: I was wondering if you could …
entries.gloss: past or continuous form makes a request softer

entries.term: mixed conditional: present condition → past result (If I were …, I would have …)

entries.term: if … should: If you should need anything, …

the present situation exists only because of this person or thing
a past result happened only because of this

entries.term: If not for …: If not for her help, …

entries.term: provided (that) / providing: You can go, provided you …

entries.term: as long as / so long as (= only if)

entries.term: suppose / supposing / imagine + past: Imagine if you lived …

entries.term: what if + past perfect: What if I'd said no?

only if = strict condition; if only = strong wish

entries.term: whether or not: Whether or not you agree, …

entries.term: be supposed to (reputation): It's supposed to be good

entries.term: was supposed to (failed plan): I was supposed to …, but …

entries.gloss: gives background circumstances or a reason

entries.term: there's + plural noun in speech: There's a lot of people
entries.gloss: very common in casual speech; write 'there are'
object pronouns after prepositions; 'and I' here is hypercorrection

entries.term: pronoun case in compound subjects: He and I went (not me and him)
entries.gloss: subject pronouns in subjects; 'me and him' is very informal

entries.term: compound adjective with a number: a ten-minute walk
entries.gloss: number + singular noun, hyphenated, before another noun

entries.term: every other / every few: every other day
entries.gloss: every other = alternate ones; every few + plural = at short intervals

entries.term: quite a few / quite a bit (= many / much)
entries.gloss: despite few and bit, it means a fairly large amount

entries.term: a couple + plural without of (US informal): a couple weeks
entries.gloss: American speech often drops of after a couple

entries.term: as many as / as much as + number
entries.gloss: stresses that a number or amount is surprisingly large

entries.term: much in affirmative sentences: There is much to do
entries.gloss: positive much sounds formal; speech prefers a lot of

entries.term: generic the + singular: The smartphone changed …
entries.gloss: the + singular noun for a whole class, often inventions or species

entries.term: the + adjective: the rich, the unemployed
entries.gloss: a group of people; takes a plural verb

entries.term: a / an with an uncountable + adjective: a good education
entries.gloss: a or an when an adjective or of-phrase describes a kind

entries.term: countable and uncountable senses: experience vs. an experience
entries.gloss: the meaning changes: general skill vs. a single event

entries.term: none of + singular or plural verb
entries.gloss: both are correct; the singular is more formal

entries.term: each / every + singular verb: Each of them has …
entries.gloss: each and every take a singular verb, even with of + plural

entries.term: neither of + plural noun: Neither of them is / are
entries.gloss: a singular verb is formal; a plural verb is common in speech
the verb agrees with the closer of the two subjects
'data is' in most American usage; 'data are' in formal science
singular criterion, phenomenon, hypothesis; avoid 'a criteria'
words ending in -s that take a singular verb

entries.term: amounts as singular: Ten dollars is …
entries.gloss: money, time and distance seen as one amount take a singular verb

entries.term: along with / as well as: the verb agrees with the first subject
entries.gloss: added phrases do not make the subject plural
the verb follows the noun after of; 'the majority' alone can be singular

entries.term: percentages and fractions: 60% of people are …
entries.gloss: the verb agrees with the noun after of

entries.term: a great deal of vs. a great many
entries.gloss: a great deal of + uncountable; a great many + plural
few = not many (negative); a few = some (positive)
little = not much (negative); a little = some (positive)

entries.term: whom in formal English: to whom, for whom
entries.gloss: object form; needed after prepositions in formal writing

entries.term: whose for things: a company whose profits …
entries.gloss: whose can refer to things, not only to people

entries.term: all vs. whole: the whole day / all day
entries.gloss: whole with singular countable nouns; all with uncountables and plurals

entries.term: hyphenated compound adjectives: a well-known author / she is well known
entries.gloss: hyphen before a noun; usually no hyphen after the verb

entries.term: noun + noun vs. 's vs. of: the car door, the company's success
entries.gloss: noun modifier for types; 's for owners; of for parts

entries.term: double possessive: a friend of mine
entries.gloss: of + possessive for one of several

entries.term: time possessive: a week's notice, two years' experience
entries.gloss: 's or s' to express a length of time
'than me' is normal; 'than I am' is careful style

entries.term: misused myself: Contact John or myself
entries.gloss: use me unless the subject is also I

entries.term: the with geographic names: the Netherlands, the Alps
entries.gloss: the with plural names, rivers, mountain ranges and some countries

entries.term: institution nouns: in the hospital (US), go to college
entries.gloss: American English: the with hospital; college with no article

entries.term: adjective + a + noun after so / too / how: too big a risk
entries.gloss: so, too, as or how + adjective + a + noun

entries.term: quite a + noun: That's quite a story
entries.gloss: a remarkable or unusual example of something

entries.term: kind of / sort of agreement: these kinds of things
entries.gloss: this kind of / these kinds of; avoid 'these kind of' in writing

entries.term: any (= no matter which): Any student can …
entries.gloss: stressed any means every one, without exception

dropped_duplicates.term: it's not that …, it's just that …
